name: Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse
tagline: T-SQL warehouse in Microsoft Fabric that stores every table as Delta Parquet in OneLake.
description: Fabric Data Warehouse is the SQL engine inside Microsoft Fabric, the SaaS analytics suite that bundles data engineering, real-time analytics and Power BI on a single capacity. It is the successor to Synapse dedicated pools: a distributed engine (from the Polaris project) that runs full T-SQL with multi-table transactions, while storing every table as open Delta Lake Parquet in OneLake so Spark notebooks and Power BI Direct Lake read the same files without copying. It suits Microsoft shops consolidating BI and warehousing; capacity-based billing and a fast-moving feature set are the trade-offs.

pricing.notes: Billed by Fabric capacity units shared across all Fabric workloads; reserved capacity discounts; 60-day trial capacity.

scale.notes: Compute is allocated automatically within the purchased Fabric capacity; storage in OneLake scales independently.

strengths: Tables are open Delta Parquet in OneLake, readable by Spark and Power BI Direct Lake
Full T-SQL with multi-table ACID transactions, familiar to SQL Server teams
No clusters or distributions to configure; compute is allocated automatically
Single capacity covers warehousing, Spark, pipelines and Power BI
Zero-copy table clones and time travel queries
weaknesses: Capacity-unit billing is hard to attribute and can throttle under bursts
T-SQL surface is still narrower than SQL Server (e.g. no triggers, limited types)
Azure-only, tied to the wider Fabric/Power BI licensing model
Younger product with frequent changes and preview features
useCases: Power BI backends with Direct Lake
Medallion lakehouse with a SQL serving layer
